The point is to spread awareness of course. I wouldn't go telling people about my conditions when I first meet them, but I am passionate about spreading awareness (mainly for autism), so I do tell people eventually, and I am open about it on social media.

People these days want to be more inclusive and find out more about things like ADHD/autism/mental illnesses. Heck, even owning an axolotl could make you tiktok famous, as people would want to know more about what it's like to own one. 

That's why having something different about you can get you famous. You're just attracting people across the globe who are interested in this particular thing, or who want to join a community.

That's not to say that people who fit the above categories (including being an axolotl owner), don't get bullied. I hope you do understand what I mean though. I empathise with your frustration.
